items.title: Paul Barbarin Interview, 1957-03-27
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] What was Longhead Bob's last name? [INTERVIEWEE] Oh, I think his name was Thompson, I think. Bob Thompson, I think it was it.

ctx.x: No, so I went to work at St. Charles Hotel. I was running the freight elevator there. And I get paid every two weeks. So my mother knew I wanted to set a drum, so she said, well, let's put the money aside. So at one time I had enough to make a down payment. So we go over to Glenwall, where my father dealt that to me. And the sign-ups got me a set of drums. And the same evening I got the drums, John Perdonce heard about it. He didn't have a drum to play. He played somebody's fixin' run for us, some hardman or…
What was Longhead Bob's last name?
Oh, I think his name was Thompson, I think. Bob Thompson, I think it was it. You know, Bill, we haven't talked about the minstrel shows at all.
